name: Recover Polygon (hard)
description: Zombies have found out about the Zombie Contamination level checker and managed to damage it! Now detecting the shape of their main compound will be a real challenge for Heidi. As before, a lair can be represented as a strictly convex polygon on a lattice. Each vertex of the polygon occupies a point on the lattice. However, the damaged Zombie Contamination level checker can only tell, for each cell, whether the level of Zombie Contamination for that cell is in the set {1, 2, 3} . In other words, Heidi knows all the cells of the lattice for which the Contamination level is not 0 and not 4 . Given this information, Heidi still wants to know the exact shape of the lair to rain destruction on the zombies. Help her!
input_specification: The input contains multiple test cases. The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers N and M , where N is the size of the lattice grid ( 5 ≤ N ≤ 100000 ) and M is the number of lattice points for which the Zombie Contamination level is 1, 2, or 3 ( 8 ≤ M ≤ 200000 ). The second line of each test case contains M pairs of integers x 1 , y 1 , ..., x M , y M – coordinates of the cells with Zombie Contamination level not equal to 0 nor 4. It is guaranteed that 1 ≤ x i , y i ≤ N . All pairs x i , y i are different. Cells are enumerated based on the coordinates of their upper right corner. This means that the bottommost leftmost cell that touches the origin has coordinates (1, 1) , and the uppermost leftmost cell is identified as (1, N ) . The last line of the file contains two zeroes. This line should not be treated as a test case. The sum of the M values for all tests in one file will not exceed 200000 .
output_specification: For each test case, the following output is expected: The first line of the output should contain one integer V , the number of vertices of the polygon that is the secret lair. The next V lines each should contain two integers, denoting the vertices of the polygon in the clockwise order, starting from the lexicographically smallest vertex.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 690B3 — Recover Polygon (hard) [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
